heroCommands.comment: Turn your coding agent into a tutor

heroCommands.command:
git clone https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch.git
cd ai-engineering-from-scratch
python3 phases/00-setup-and-tooling/01-dev-environment/code/verify.py --route beginner

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: AI Engineering from Scratch is a free, open course where you implement model internals, retrieval pipelines and agent runtimes yourself, then test and inspect them. It has 542 lessons in 20 phases, in Python, TypeScript, Rust, Julia and Go.
sixtySeconds.problem: Framework calls hide the part that breaks. By writing small versions of each piece, such as a ReAct loop in plain Python, you learn where to look when a loss turns into NaN or an agent loops on the same tool call.
whoFor: Learners who prefer building over reading
Claude Code and Codex users who want an AI tutor
People preparing for AI engineering roles
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a large, hands-on, from-scratch curriculum you can follow on the website, with a coding agent as tutor, or by running code locally. It is free and MIT licensed.
requirements: A web browser for the website
Python 3 (3.10+ for projects) to run lessons
Optional: Node.js and a skill-capable coding agent for the tutor
Node.js 22.18+ and Rust for some projects

overview: Lessons follow a pattern: the problem, build it from scratch, see where real SDKs do the same thing, then ship a reusable artifact such as a skill file for your agent. Learning routes start from model foundations, LLM systems or agents and delivery.

You can learn on the website with no setup, install the course as skills so your coding agent becomes a tutor (with a placement quiz and one lesson per session), or clone the repository and run lesson code. A preflight script checks your environment and suggests fixes.

Three graded projects have staged starters, reference solutions and local graders: a retrieval evaluation lab in Python, an agent trace debugger in TypeScript and a tool call firewall in Rust. The course is translated into many languages.
